pairs.question: Quaero, an titia, quae non appellavit adversus sententiam praesidis, possit ad falsi accusationem postea reverti.
pairs.answer: Respondit nihil aperte proponi, propter quod adversus sententiae auctoritatem de falso agens audienda sit.
pairs.derivation: Within the consilium of 48.2.18, the consultant's question is introduced verbatim by 'quaero, an...'; the jurist's reply follows immediately with 'respondit'. I drop the preceding narrative setup (the Titia/falsum facts) because the question 'an...possit ad falsi accusationem postea reverti' is self-contained. The answer is the single sentence after 'respondit'; nothing is cut after it (next is a new section marker).

pairs.question: Mulier cum absentem virum audisset vita functum esse, alii se iunxit: mox maritus reversus est. Quaero, quid adversus eam mulierem statuendum sit.
pairs.answer: Respondit tam iuris quam facti quaestionem moveri: nam si longo tempore transacto sine ullius stupri probatione falsis rumoribus inducta, quasi soluta priore vinculo, legitimis nuptiis secundis iuncta est, quod verisimile est deceptam eam fuisse nihil vindicta dignum videri potest.
pairs.derivation: I keep the factual setup ('Mulier cum... reversus est') because it gives the referent for 'eam mulierem'; this setup is verbatim source text. The interrogative is 'quaero, quid... statuendum sit'. For the answer I stop at the first full stop of the operative reply ('...nihil vindicta dignum videri potest'); the reply then continues with the contrasting 'quod si ficta mariti mors...' which is a separate branch, so I cut there.

pairs.question: Ream adulterii uxorem duxi: eam damnatam mox repudiavi. Quaero, an causam discidii praestitisse videor.
pairs.answer: Respondit: cum per legem iuliam huiusmodi uxorem retinere prohibearis, non videri causam te discidii praestitisse palam est.
pairs.derivation: The first-person setup ('Ream... repudiavi') is kept verbatim so 'causam discidii' has its referent; the question is 'quaero, an...videor'. The answer is the reply up to its first full stop; the following sentence ('quare ita ius tractabitur...') is a consequence and is cut.

pairs.question: Quaesitum est, an ea, quam maritus adulterii crimine se accusaturum minatus est nec quicquam egit vel iure mariti vel iure publico, nubere possit ei, quem in ea reum adulterii destinavit.
pairs.answer: Paulus respondit nihil impedire, quo minus ei, quem suspectum maritus habuit, ea de qua quaeritur nubere possit.
pairs.derivation: Clean responsum: the question is introduced 'Quaesitum est, an...' and answered by 'Paulus respondit...'. The question is self-contained. Answer ends at the full stop; next is a new section.

pairs.question: Quaesitum est, an is, qui libello principi dato falsum se obiecturum minatus est, si non obiecisset, turpilliano senatus consulto tenetur.
pairs.answer: Paulus respondit verbis senatus consulti turpilliani eum de quo quaeritur non contineri.
pairs.derivation: Clean responsum. Question opens 'Quaesitum est, an...'; answer is the whole 'Paulus respondit...' sentence, self-contained, nothing cut after.

pairs.question: Lucius titius seium reum falsi fecit et priusquam persequeretur, indulgentia reorum crimina abolita sunt. Quaero, si postea eum iterato reum non fecerit, an in turpillianum senatus consultum inciderit.
pairs.answer: Herennius modestinus respondit abolitionem reorum, quae publice indulgetur, ad hoc genus criminis non pertinere.
pairs.derivation: The factual setup ('Lucius titius... abolita sunt') is kept verbatim because it supplies the referents ('eum', 'iterato reum') for the question; the interrogative is 'quaero, si... an... inciderit'. Answer is the full 'Herennius modestinus respondit...' sentence.

pairs.question: Unde quaeri potest, an is, qui de adulterio cognoscit, statuere in maritum ob lenocinium possit?
pairs.derivation: Self-posed question (Ulpianus) marked by 'an... possit?', answered immediately by 'et puto posse'. I drop the framing 'Unde quaeri potest' only insofar as it narrates the asking—but here it is grammatically fused to the 'an'-clause, so I retain it as part of the verbatim utterance. The answer stops at 'et puto posse'; what follows ('nam claudius gorgus...') is a supporting example, cut.

pairs.question: Si publico iudicio maritus uxorem ream faciat, an lenocinii allegatio repellat maritum ab accusatione?
pairs.answer: Et putem non repellere: lenocinium igitur mariti ipsum onerat, non mulierem excusat.
pairs.derivation: Self-posed question with conditional setup kept verbatim ('Si publico iudicio... ream faciat') plus the interrogative 'an... repellat... ?'. Answer is 'et putem non repellere' plus its immediate explanatory clause to the full stop; this is the whole remainder of the paragraph, nothing cut after.

pairs.question: Stuprum in sororis filiam si committatur, an adulterii poena sufficiat mari, considerandum est.
pairs.answer: Occurrit, quod hic duplex admissum est, quia multum interest, errore matrimonium illicite contrahatur an contumacia iuris et sanguinis contumelia concurrant.
pairs.derivation: Author poses the question ('an adulterii poena sufficiat mari') and answers it himself with 'Occurrit, quod hic duplex admissum est...'. The conditional setup is kept verbatim. Answer runs to the end of the paragraph (its single full stop).
